title: Anomaly Detection Across 5G Slices Using Federated Learning
summary: An Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad team reports that its cross-slice federated learning model reached a macro F1 score of 93.83% on a test dataset with new anomalous traffic.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: A team at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad develops the system with open-source network tools and network emulators. It is intended to identify anomalies across 5G network slices while the data stay distributed. In October 2025 the IIT Hyderabad team reported at the MSWiM conference in Barcelona that its cross-slice federated model reached a macro F1 score of 93.83% on a test dataset with new anomalous traffic. The authors are the developers. No source reports use in an operator network. No source reports an intercepted attack, a prevented loss or a measured service improvement.
purpose: Detect network anomalies across distributed 5G slices.
system: Anomaly Detection Across 5G Slices Using Federated Learning

ratings.reason: The federated model has a detection score on a test dataset, and no source reports that it intercepted a threat in an operating network.
